card.hook: Legend says a peasant girl found a tiny figure of the Virgin Mary right here in Cartago. Now there's a whole basilica of towers, domes and carved doorways built around her story.
card.stand_here: Stand near Avenida Central, about 20 m west of the numbered pin, at the phone icon on the map, and face east. The middle of the basilica outline is about 21 m ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to squeeze in the whole building, then go to 1x for a more natural look. Try 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) for towers, windows and carved stonework.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up the towers with the vertical lines so the building doesn't lean, and hold your phone upright and level.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters a big building like this, and thin cloud helps by softening the shadows.
card.selfie_here: Head to the open park and plaza in front of the basilica, on the Avenida Central and Avenida Primera side. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the church behind you, over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos are allowed inside, but skip the flash and be respectful of people praying. It's a place of worship, so dress respectfully and check the official site for visiting times and any rules.
card.challenge: Find a doorway or carved detail, then wait for a passer-by to walk through so we can see just how big this place really is.
card.good_to_know: The first basilica was built in 1639 and was partly destroyed by an earthquake. It was restored, and the building you see today dates from 1939. It mixes colonial architecture with 19th-century Byzantine style, which is why there's so much detail to photograph.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand near Avenida Central, about 20 m west of the numbered pin, at the phone icon on the map, and face east. The middle of the basilica outline is about 21 m ahead of you.

selfie_research.notes: Only one selfie spot was confirmed with a page naming a place where the basilica can be behind the photographed visitor; the 'park in front' description comes from nytocostarica.com, which mentions a lawn and fountain from an older visit (around 1984), so the current layout may differ. A second candidate, the outside holy-water fountain (Fuente del Agua Bendita), is named by the Tico Times, but no page places it relative to the facade, so I left it out. The parking-area spot is a photographer's vantage point named in a blog post, not a recommended spot for passers-by. No page gave selfie-stick or tripod rules.

card.hook: Picture weathered stone walls with plants poking out and a big sky behind them. The Ruinas de Santiago Apóstol hand you that shot almost for free.
card.stand_here: Head for the phone icon near Avenida Central, about 50 m north of the ruins. Face south and the whole structure is straight ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural view of the whole ruin. If you're close and it won't fit, drop to 0.5x. Then try zoom 2x or more (depending on your phone) for stonework details without walking closer.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the ruins, then slide the picture a bit darker if the sky is washed out, so the sky keeps its colour and the stone still shows.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon gives softer light and fewer people. Midday sun can be harsh on pale stone, and cloud or rain will change the mood, so check the weather.
card.selfie_here: Try beside the small ponds in the inner garden, with the stone walls and curved arches behind you. Use the front camera, hold it a little low and try 0.5x so the arches fit over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand on the far side of the street to the north and frame the north face with the roadside garden in front, so the whole ruin fits in the shot with you in it.
card.rules_and_safety: Rules for entering the grounds can change, and entry has sometimes not been allowed, so check locally before you go, especially for the garden.
card.challenge: Find an arch or doorway and frame the ruin through it, then take one wide shot and one close-up of the stone.
card.good_to_know: These are the ruins of a building named after Saint James the Apostle, in Cartago. The weathered stone gives you strong shapes and textures, and the contrast with greenery and sky makes photos look layered. Wipe your phone lens first, because a smudge really shows against bright sky.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for the phone icon near Avenida Central, about 50 m north of the ruins. Face south and the whole structure is straight ahead of you.

selfie_research.notes: Only one selfie spot was confirmed with a named location; I found no page naming a second selfie spot with the landmark behind the visitor (the 'stone arches framing the sky' tip has no location). The Texas photo is an undated archive image of visitors, not a selfie guide. The Tripadvisor 'across the street' suggestion comes from reviewer photo notes, not an official guide. The Worldwide Panorama page lists coordinates (84°56' W) that do not match the given position, so I did not rely on it. One 2016 Foursquare review says entry was sometimes not allowed, which may matter for the garden spot; it is a single, old comment.
